description: TanStack Query-inspired async data fetching and state management for .NET, Blazor, and MVVM apps, built on Rx.NET.
rules: Set QueryExecutionMode.Ssr in AddFetchling for Blazor Server / SSR so IQueryClient is scoped per circuit; the default Csr registers it as a singleton.
Query TData must be a reference type; wrap value types in a record or class.
Dispose queries and view models when their owner is torn down: a live subscription pins the cache entry indefinitely.
In MVVM, use ObserveOnUi() for the Success/Failure/Settled event streams; the bindable view model properties coalesce latest-wins and would drop events.
Call MutationViewModel.ToCommand once per command, typically in a constructor, never per list row.
IQueryClient.Invalidate(QueryKey) matches the key exactly, not as a prefix; pass a predicate such as key => key.Parts is ["todos", ..] to invalidate a group.
Invalidate (and a mutation's InvalidateKeys) refetches observed queries regardless of StaleTime; use IQueryClient.InvalidateStale(predicate) for a sweep that should leave fresh data alone.

A streamed query over a never-ending stream (SignalR, SSE) never settles: render from State, not Success; don't PrefetchAsync it; set CancelWhenUnobservedAfter (e.g. 2 s), or the stream stays open until eviction.
In tests, register a TestScheduler as the IScheduler to drive stale time, cache eviction, and refetch intervals in virtual time.
